accept_min.bin.note: Smallest legal frame (07 §5 lower bound: len > 0). Also the designated split-iteration vector — see README §Split iteration.

accept_two_frames.bin.note: Two frames in one buffer; distinct payload lengths so an off-by-one in 'consumed' cannot cancel out. Also split-iterated — see README §Split iteration.

accept_max_len.bin.note: len == M1PL_MAX_FRAME exactly (08 §4.2) — the bound is inclusive; a decoder written as 'len >= MAX' fails here.

accept_then_reject.bin.note: Valid frame followed by a full 9-byte garbage header (magic 'XXXX', rest well-formed): accept frame 1, then reject — never silently discard an unparseable tail (12 §3.4 row 6). Never scan forward for the next valid magic (12 §3.4 row 1).

accept_then_incomplete_tail.bin.note: 12 §3.4 row 6 literal: valid frame + 3 undecodable bytes. Under the header-buffered decoder model (README §Decoder model) a <9-byte remainder is 'incomplete'; EOF while incomplete is a connection error, not a flush (12 §3.4 row 5) — so the stream-level result is accept-then-error as the doc requires.

incomplete_payload.bin.note: Header complete and valid (len=4) but only 3 payload bytes present. Never surface a partial Event; EOF in this state is an error, not a flush (12 §3.4 row 5).

reject_bad_magic.bin.note: Magic 'M1Pl' — only the LAST magic byte is wrong (0x6C not 0x4C), rest identical to accept_min.bin, so a 3-byte magic compare fails here. Code per 12 §3.4 row 1.

reject_ver_00.bin.note: ver below the shipped set; no partial-parse fallback (12 §3.4 row 2). Code per 08 §7 error table (version mismatch).

reject_ver_02.bin.note: ver above the shipped set; no 'try v1 anyway' (12 §3.4 row 2).

reject_len_zero.bin.note: len == 0 is a desynchronized stream, not an empty Event — the half a decoder written as 'if len > MAX' silently omits (08 §4.2, 12 §3.4 row 3). Header-only file: a zero-length frame has no payload bytes.

reject_len_over.bin.note: len == M1PL_MAX_FRAME + 1. Header-only file BY DESIGN: the decoder must reject from the 9-byte header without seeing, needing, or allocating for any payload byte (12 §3.4 row 4 — 'reject before allocating').
